objective: Compare constrained numeric length properties and return the exact selected argument with explicit strict-comparison semantics.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Generic constraints and structural numeric properties remain current TypeScript foundations.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Choosing an existing longer value is a small practical selector.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Returning the original T and distinguishing strict comparison from its complement transfer to other comparisons.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: Two stable length reads isolate the foundational constraint objective.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Cloning a generic return or complementing comparisons around NaN can change the promised selection.

defects: Exact selected-reference identity and raw numeric-length policy were unstated.
Senior used a>=b as a complement to b>a, disagreeing for unordered NaN comparisons.
Cloning the selected object/array passed all old value-only cases.
rationale: Retain reference/junior and change senior to the stated strict b.length>a.length test. Define stable data length properties on strings/arrays/functions/records, no traversal/coercion/calls/mutation and exact original return. Make NaN fallback explicit: b is returned only when the strict comparison is true; ties or unordered comparisons keep a. Numeric infinities and signed zero follow Number comparison, and text length is UTF-16. Cases inspect frozen ties/winners, NaN on either side, infinity/signed-zero ties, inherited negative fractional lengths, uncalled functions, Unicode text and array identity. Static evidence retains extra fields. Target constant property/comparison work.
